approach: Three changes where the fault starts, plus a neutral brief wording. (1) Driver (claude.rs): split `ClaudeCodeDriver::invoke` into a private `invoke_once` and a wrapper. When the first call ends as an error result whose detail is an API Error 401, the wrapper treats both calls as ONE invocation. A pure helper `retry_spec` works out what is left of the spec: timeout minus (first run plus wait), budget minus the first call's reported cost; it returns None (no retry, return the first output) when under 10 s or under $0.01 is left. Otherwise the wrapper waits (injectable `auth_retry_wait`, default 30 s, polled in 1 s slices against the kill switch), prepends one line to the prompt ("An earlier attempt at this task stopped when the login expired. Anything it changed is already in your working directory: check it before redoing work."), runs `invoke_once` with the reduced spec through a sink that adds the first call's totals on top of the second call's, and returns one merged AgentOutput (usage, cost, models_used, turns, duration_api_ms, commands_run, denials summed or concatenated; started_at from the first call, ended_at from the second, wall_s measured over the pair; outcome, detail and structured from the second). `api_error_status` moves from disk.rs into athena-agent so the driver and `StopCause::of` share one parser. (2) Keep-work: in producer.rs a producer failure whose StopCause is ProducerAuth calls `keep_unfinished_work` (renamed, generalised `keep_timed_out_work`), which builds the candidate commit and progress note as the deadline path does, leaves the job Failed with the `environment: producer login expired: ...` reason plus `; its edits are kept as candidate <short>`. All other failures (429 included) still go to `self.failure` and keep nothing. (3) Resume: `timeout_seed` accepts a Closed(TimedOut) job or a Closed(Failed) job with a login-expiry reason through a new `disk::keeps_unfinished_work`; the retry then uses the existing seed path. No resume mark is written. The Resume section of the producer brief (briefs.rs) is reworded neutrally so it no longer says the earlier producer reached its deadline.

decisions.choice: Make the driver's two calls act as one invocation: reduced remaining timeout and budget for the second call, a sink that adds the first call's totals, and one merged AgentOutput.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 1. claude.rs:350 computes the deadline inside each call, so a plain second call would get a fresh producer_timeout_s and the full budget. FileSink::update (core invocation.rs:75-81) overwrites the stored partial usage with the latest totals, and only one AgentOutput reaches invoke_and_record. The incident's first call ran 30 minutes, so its spend is large and must be counted. Merging in the driver keeps caps, the partial-usage file and the invocation record true, and the core stays unaware of the retry. If the first call fails to leave time or budget, the first output is returned and the core makes the environment stop.

rejected.option: Return only the second call's output (previous plan).
rejected.why: Drops the first call's cost and usage and doubles the time and budget caps.

rejected.option: Do the retry in core's invoke_and_record.
rejected.why: The brief puts it in claude.rs, and a core retry would also hit the fake driver, hiding the stop the core test must show.

rejected.option: Sum cost in the core from two recorded invocations.
rejected.why: Needs a second record and seq per call, a record-format change outside the listed files.

decisions.choice: Cost is summed only when both calls reported one; otherwise the merged cost is None (so the record shows it as bounded by the original cap). usage_measured is true only when both calls measured.
decisions.reason: A killed or timed-out second call has no reported cost; recording the first call's cost alone as 'reported' would under-count. None makes invocation_record use cost_bounded_by_cap with the spec's original cap, and the second call's cap is the original minus the first call's cost, so the bound holds.

rejected.option: Treat a missing second cost as zero.
rejected.why: Records a reported cost that is a known under-count.

decisions.choice: On the retry, prepend a one-line note to the user prompt saying an earlier attempt was cut off by an expired login and its edits are in the working directory.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 2. The CLI runs with --no-session-persistence (claude.rs:30), so the model cannot remember its earlier edits; the note tells it to check the tree before redoing work. It is neutral for read-only roles (anything it changed).

rejected.option: Name the limit only in the CHANGELOG.
rejected.why: The model would still redo or contradict work; one line in the prompt is cheaper.

decisions.choice: Reword the Resume section in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs:572 to 'That job's producer stopped before it finished (a deadline or an environment stop; the note below says which).' and list briefs.rs as a file.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 3. The strangers default and the model's trust in the brief forbid a false cause. The change is one sentence; `a_resume_brief_carries_the_progress_note` (briefs.rs:1790) checks the heading, 'kept as candidate', 'what the plan still needs' and the quoted note, not 'reached its deadline', so it stays valid and gets one added assertion that the brief no longer says 'reached its deadline'.

rejected.option: Leave the wording and rely on the quoted note.
rejected.why: The brief would state a false cause.

rejected.option: Pass the cause into RetrySeed and word it per cause.
rejected.why: Needs a new RetrySeed field and changes in core; the neutral sentence is enough.

decisions.choice: Reuse the deadline's keep-work function for a login expiry (renamed `keep_unfinished_work`, with an `Ended::{Deadline, EnvironmentStop}` parameter) and extend `timeout_seed` to a Failed job with a login-expiry reason. Write no resume mark.
decisions.reason: A deadline and a login expiry both leave a partly done tree. The timeout path already builds the candidate, progress note and brief, and a retry already resumes the producer from them (producer.rs:136, run/mod.rs:1162 and 1288). With no resume mark, `resume_seed` stays None, so the retry runs a producer on the partial work.

rejected.why: resume_candidate runs no producer and goes to checks and the verifier; it would verify unfinished work.

rejected.option: Close a login-expired producer as TimedOut.
rejected.why: StopCause::of and resumable_stop would no longer see an environment stop; the scope guard would count it as work and the drain would not end the batch.

decisions.reason: athena-agent cannot depend on athena-core (core depends on agent). One parser means the driver retries exactly what the core classifies as a login expiry.

decisions.choice: Only a 401 keeps work and only a 401 is retried by the driver. 429, low disk and other errors behave as today.
decisions.reason: The request puts 429 handling out of scope; criterion 6 requires the 429 and low-disk paths unchanged.

rejected.option: Keep work for every environment stop.

decisions.choice: If `athena stop` turns the kill switch on during the wait, the wrapper returns Err(DriverError::Stopped), as the start of invoke_once does.
decisions.reason: Same contract as a stop before a call. The first call's updates already sit in the partial-usage file (FileSink persists after every event and is removed only by finish()), so its spend is still counted by close.

rejected.why: Would close the job as a login expiry while the owner asked for a stop.

risks.risk: The retried call starts a new conversation (the CLI runs with --no-session-persistence, claude.rs:30), so the model does not remember the edits it made before the 401 and may redo them.
risks.mitigation: The retry prompt is prefixed with a line saying an earlier attempt stopped when the login expired and that anything it changed is already in the working directory, to check it before redoing work. The send-back, format step, checks and verifier still judge the final tree. If the retry fails too, the 401 stop keeps the tree and the progress note for `athena retry`.

risks.risk: The retry could exceed the job's caps (a fresh timeout and budget) or lose the first call's spend.
risks.mitigation: The second call gets the remaining timeout and budget from `retry_spec`; when under 10 s or $0.01 is left, no retry is made and the first output is returned. Usage, cost, models, commands and turns of both calls are merged into one output, and the sink adds the first call's totals. Tests cover the sums, the remainder and the skip.

risks.risk: A 30 s wait may be shorter than the time the login takes to refresh (the incident says minutes).
risks.mitigation: The brief asks for a short wait and one retry. If the login is still expired the job stops as an environment stop with its work kept and `athena retry` resumes it. The wait is one constant.

risks.risk: `athena stop` during the wait could hold a worker or start another call.
risks.mitigation: The wait sleeps in one-second slices and checks `registry.stopped()`, returning DriverError::Stopped as the start of `invoke_once` does; the first call's usage stays in the partial-usage file. Test `an_athena_stop_during_a_login_expiry_wait_ends_the_retry`. Tests use a 300 ms wait.

risks.risk: If the second call is killed or times out its cost is unknown, so the merged cost is None and the record shows a bounded estimate, not the first call's known spend.
risks.mitigation: This is the same representation a single killed call gets today (cost_bounded_by_cap). The cap used is the original budget, and the second call's cap is the original minus the first's cost, so the bound is not exceeded.

risks.risk: `api_error_status` moves between crates and `keep_timed_out_work` is renamed.
risks.mitigation: Searched the crates: `api_error_status` is used only in disk.rs (production at 485 and 503, tests at 1387, 1430, 1444) and `keep_timed_out_work` only at producer.rs:381 and its definition. No `include_str!` or file read of a moved file applies, since no file moves. Step 1 re-checks with Grep before editing.

risks.risk: The drain's retry of a 401 item now resumes from partial work and the first attempt's edits may be wrong.
risks.mitigation: This is the requested behaviour, the same as a timed-out item today. The resumed producer is told to check the kept edits, and checks and the verifier judge the result.

demonstrations.method: New test `a_producer_login_expiry_keeps_its_edits_and_closes_as_an_environment_stop` in crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs. demonstrations.method: New tests in the `stand_in_tests` module of crates/athena-agent/src/claude.rs, using the real `ClaudeCodeDriver::invoke` and a real child process. The existing STAND_IN shell script is extended: it reads the prompt into the file named by env PROMPT_FILE (default /dev/null), counts calls in the file named by env COUNT_FILE and appends each call's arguments to `$COUNT_FILE.args`; new modes `auth_once` (call 1 prints a 401 result with subtype `success`, is_error true, `total_cost_usd` 0.25, usage and modelUsage entries; later calls print the normal success result), `auth_always`, `auth_stop` (writes STOP_FILE, then prints the 401 result) and `limit` (a 429 result). Test `a_login_expiry_is_retried_once_and_a_second_call_succeeds`: driver from the module's `driver()` helper with `auth_retry_wait` set to 300 ms, spec timeout 30 s and budget 0.5, `COUNT_FILE` and `PROMPT_FILE` in `spec.env`. Asserts: outcome Success; `structured["answer"] == 42`; count file reads 2; elapsed at least 300 ms; the second call's arguments carry `--max-budget-usd 0.25` (0.5 minus the first call's 0.25); the second prompt contains the expired-login note and the original `brief`; returned `cost_usd` is the sum (0.25 + 0.002, within 1e-9), `usage` is the sum of both calls, `commands_run` holds both calls' commands, `models_used` is merged, and the recorder sink's last update equals the summed usage. Test `a_login_expiry_with_no_time_left_is_not_retried`: timeout 2 s, wait 3 s gives count 1 and the first Error output returned. Test `an_athena_stop_during_a_login_expiry_wait_ends_the_retry`: mode `auth_stop` returns Err(DriverError::Stopped) with count 1. Test `a_usage_limit_is_not_retried`: mode `limit` gives count 1 and an Error output. Pure test `retry_spec_leaves_the_remaining_time_and_budget`: for spec timeout 600 s, first run 100 s and wait 30 s the retry spec's timeout is 470 s (under a 10 s remainder gives None), budget is original minus first cost (under $0.01 gives None), and the prompt starts with the note and ends with the original prompt.
demonstrations.observes: The first call returns a 401 error result, the driver waits, the second call succeeds, the stand-in's call count is exactly 2, the returned output carries both calls' spend, the second call ran with the remaining budget and the note, and the retry is skipped when no time is left, on a stop, and for a 429.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the wrapper the first call's 401 Error is returned: outcome is Error and the count is 1, so the Success and count assertions fail. Without the merge, cost_usd would be 0.002 and the sum assertion fails. Without the remainder logic the second call's `--max-budget-usd` is 0.50 and the args assertion fails.
